Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
This looks like a period of high policy rates after rapid hikes, with inflation falling from its peak. The fed funds rate is high (+3.0) and rose over 3 months (+1.5) and 12 months (+2.5), so hikes are still ongoing. CPI is falling (3m change -1.5), the dollar is down over 3 months (-1.5), and the stock-bond correlation is positive. Together these point to late 2022 through early 2023.

Against the 36-month window, the policy rate being at +3.0 and up +2.5 over 12 months fits late 2022 or early 2023. The 12m equity return of -1.5 fits the 12 months to Oct–Dec 2022, and developed ex-US equity 3m of +2.0 fits a rally from the Oct 2022 low. The 1m US equity return of -1.0 fits December 2022, when the S&P fell about 5.8%. The dollar's 3m change of -1.5 also fits, since it peaked in September 2022. The 10y yield 3m change of -0.5 fits too, because the 10y was around 3.9% in December against 3.8% in September. Gold's 3m return of +1.0 fits as well.

Unemployment at -0.5 is consistent with 3.5%. I pick December 2022.
